Let’s dive into Chapter 7: Advanced Techniques—Calibrating and Testing Your Impressions.
Now, once you’ve got the basics down and you’re aware of your own biases, it’s time to take things a step further. This is where calibration and gentle testing come in. Think of it as moving from simply watching what happens, to actually checking—kindly and respectfully—if your gut feeling matches reality.
So, what exactly is calibration? Imagine tuning a guitar. Just a tiny tweak can make the notes sound clear and true. Calibration works the same way for your perceptions. It’s all about comparing what you think is going on, with what’s actually happening—and then making those little adjustments.
One great way to do this is by asking for feedback. And you don’t have to overthink it! Maybe you notice someone seemed quiet in a meeting. Instead of guessing, you could say, “Hey, I noticed you seemed a little quiet today—was everything okay?” It’s a gentle approach that shows you care, and it gives the other person a chance to clarify.
Next, pay close attention to how people respond. If they open up and start sharing, chances are your impression was on track. But if they pull away or seem uncomfortable, it might be time to rethink your interpretation.
And here’s the key—use what you learn to adjust how you interact, and how you understand the situation.
Now, let’s talk about testing your impressions, which is really about the gentle probe. No, you’re not interrogating anyone! Instead, you’re creating safe moments for people to share more about how they feel or what they’re thinking.
For example, simply offering support—like asking, “Is there anything I can help with?”—might encourage someone to open up. Or, you could use hypotheticals. Try asking, “How would you feel if…?” That way, you give someone space to express themselves without feeling like they’re under a microscope.
Here’s a real-life example. Let’s say a friend seems distant. Instead of assuming they’re upset with you, you might gently say, “You’ve seemed a bit off lately—anything on your mind?” That small question opens the door for an honest conversation and lets you recalibrate your understanding based on what they share.
Remember, calibration and testing are really about staying flexible and open. People are complex—always changing. By regularly checking in on your impressions, you build trust and avoid getting stuck in assumptions.
So, next time you’re unsure about what someone’s feeling, try a little calibration and a gentle test. It’s amazing how much clarity and connection it can bring.
